### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No journal-specific AI clause found. The guidelines page (snapshot 2024-09-27) only states that AI chatbots such as ChatGPT must not be listed as authors and points to Sage's publisher policy |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No prior-permission step in the Sage policy as read; disclosure is required for generative uses |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Sage publisher policy (Wayback snapshot of 2026-11-15, read 2026-11-23): AI used to improve language, grammar or structure is "assistive" and needs no disclosure. Generative use that touches research methodology, analysis, results or conclusions must be disclosed at submission, in methods or acknowledgements; listed examples are literature-review assistance, translation, AI-generated code, data visualisation, illustrations and reference compilation. Authors must verify every output and cite original sources rather than the AI tool. Disclosed use alone does not cause rejection; undisclosed inappropriate use can lead the editor to reject at any stage. Inappropriate uses named: fabricated text, data or references, AI "interviews" in place of participants, AI analysis of themes, plagiarism, and AI images presented as original. Reviewers may use GenAI to help write or format a report but stay responsible for it; editors must not use GenAI for decision letters or summaries of unpublished work |
| **Source URL** | https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy |

| **Reference limit** | None stated. A reference list with consistent citations is required; notes numbered consecutively and placed at the end, double spaced. The named citation style is not reliably readable in the snapshot (several Sage style sentences appear together), so it is left blank |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed; hosted online alongside the article |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit stated. Figures numbered consecutively, 300 dpi; permission needed for reproduced material |

| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Method vocabulary is almost absent: "interview" 2 (0.4%), "qualitative" 1 (0.2%), "quantitative|statistic*" 2 (0.4%), "survey|questionnaire" 3 (0.6%), "ethnograph*" 3 (0.6%) |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** the aims page says the journal presents "an international range of theory and critique" and emphasises "the contribution of continental scholarship" (https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/psc, snapshot 2022-11-25). The home page of 2025 describes "original theoretical contributions to the latest developments in social and political thought" (https://journals.sagepub.com/home/psc, snapshot 2025-06-26). The 2026-11-23 Crossref sample is consistent: recent items include reconsiderations of Schopenhauer as a political thinker (DOI 10.1177/01914537261481247), council democracy (10.1177/01914537261481246), recognition and sexual subjectivity (10.1177/01914537261484989) and Adorno on social inertia (10.1177/01914537261481242).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** theoretical and critical essays; historical-genealogical argument (104 abstracts, 20.9%); textual interpretation of canonical thinkers; normative political philosophy (71, 14.3%); comparative and cross-tradition work (an earlier pass noted a Han Fei article and a Lefort article; Lefort appears in 9 abstracts).

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

- Scope statement: the aims page says the journal wishes to provide a forum for open scholarly discussion of its themes "from a critical-historical point of view" (a description of the forum's own perspective, not a stated requirement on authors) and emphasises continental scholarship (https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/psc, snapshot 2022-11-25). It states no political party or school line.
- Named thinkers in titles/abstracts of 498 articles with abstracts, 2021-2026 (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23): Adorno 31 (6.2%), Marx 28 (5.6%), Hegel 27 (5.4%), Foucault 26 (5.2%), Rawls 25 (5.0%), Arendt 23 (4.6%), Habermas 23 (4.6%), Kant 23 (4.6%), Schmitt 15 (3.0%), Honneth 12 (2.4%), Rancière 10 (2.0%), Derrida 9 (1.8%), Lefort 9 (1.8%), Nietzsche 9 (1.8%), Heidegger 5 (1.0%), Wittgenstein 3 (0.6%), Husserl 3 (0.6%).
- Traditions and terms: "democra*" 141 (28.3%), "critique" 102 (20.5%), "normative" 71 (14.3%), "recognition" 48 (9.6%), "populis*" 38 (7.6%), "Marx*" 28 (5.6%), "feminis*" 24 (4.8%), "phenomenolog*" 24 (4.8%), "postcolon*|decolon*|colonial" 20 (4.0%), "pragmati*" 18 (3.6%), "analytic" 18 (3.6%), "neoliberal*" 16 (3.2%), "continental" 4 (0.8%).
- OpenAlex topics (spine, 2026-07-13): Critical Theory and Philosophy 459 articles, Political Philosophy and Ethics 440, Hannah Arendt's Political Philosophy 210, Political Economy and Marxism 161.
- Editorial board names listed on the 2022 snapshot include Axel Honneth, Rainer Forst, Chantal Mouffe, Jodi Dean and Christoph Menke (https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/psc, snapshot 2022-11-06).
- Reading of the counts: the published work is led by Frankfurt-school and post-Kantian political thought (Adorno, Marx, Hegel, Habermas, Honneth, Rawls) with Foucault and Arendt close behind; analytic-tradition vocabulary appears at 3.6%. This describes what is published, not an editorial stance on any political question.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: the aims page defines scope as essays in philosophy and politics, philosophy and social theory, socio-economic thought, critique of science, and theory and praxis (https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/psc, snapshot 2022-11-25). The guidelines page says an out-of-scope or low-quality article "will not be reviewed" (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psc, snapshot 2024-09-27).
- Cover letter: the editor asks for a cover letter stating why the manuscript suits the journal (same page).
- Article types: original research and review articles per the home page; unsolicited book reviews are not published (guidelines page).
- 498 abstracts: 273 (54.8%) contain "argu*", and 335 of the 498 (67.3%) open or refer to "this article/paper/essay/study/chapter", so a thesis-driven argumentative frame is the norm in the sample (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Consequence of ignoring the scope: the only statement found is that out-of-scope manuscripts are not reviewed; no desk-reject rate is published (SciRev 0 reviews).

### Methodological Preferences

Scoring rule (this pass's own convention, not a journal statement): hits divided by the 498 records with abstracts; 0 gives 0, under 1% gives 1, 1-5% gives 2, over 5% gives 3. Scores of 4-5 need an editorial statement and none was found. Source: Crossref titles/abstracts for ISSN 0191-4537, 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23; counts are lower bounds.

| Theoretical / conceptual analysis | 3 | "theoretic*|conceptual" 101 articles (20.3%); capped at 3 by rule though clearly the dominant mode |

| Historical / genealogical | 3 | "histor*|genealog*" 104 articles (20.9%) |

### Voice & Style

- Abstract: unstructured, 100-150 words; keywords up to 10 or at least 5 (the page states both) (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psc, snapshot 2024-09-27).
- Format: double-spaced; notes numbered consecutively at the end; manuscripts are published in gender-neutral form (same page).
- First-person use in the 498 deposited abstracts (Crossref, 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23): "I" appears in 228 (45.8%), "we" in 124 (24.9%), "our" in 76 (15.3%), "my" in 32 (6.4%); "this article/paper/essay/study/chapter" in 335 (67.3%). First-person "I argue" is common, e.g. DOI 10.1177/01914537261484989 ("I argue that sexuality has a uniquely complex relationship to recognition").
- Ten most recent abstract openings sampled (Crossref, 2026): five begin with "This article/paper" plus a verb such as argues, traces, addresses, explores or offers (DOIs 10.1177/01914537261496517, 10.1177/01914537261481244, 10.1177/01914537261484989, 10.1177/01914537261481246, 10.1177/01914537261481252); the other five open with a general claim about the field (10.1177/01914537261481248, 10.1177/01914537261481247, 10.1177/01914537261481258), a quotation from Adorno (10.1177/01914537261481242) or a participial phrase on Heller's reading of Kant and Marx (10.1177/01914537261475361).
- Citation style: not reliably readable in the snapshot (see Format table), so no claim is made.

### Practical Concerns

- Ethics / IRB: papers reporting human participants, human data or tissue must state ethics-committee approval or waiver, with committee name and approval number; a "Statements and Declarations" section is required, with "Not applicable" where relevant (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psc, snapshot 2024-09-27). Given that interview and survey vocabulary appears in under 1% of abstracts, this will rarely apply.
- Declarations: conflict-of-interest and funding statements are required even when nothing applies; a data-availability statement is encouraged, not required (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psc).
- Authorship and third parties: AI chatbots may not be authors; third-party or ghost submission must be disclosed, and the editor may decline submissions made by a third party (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psc).
- Preprints: accepted, with the preprint DOI entered at submission (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psc); see the Preprint table.
- OA / charges: no submission or publication fee; optional OA via Sage Choice at an unstated fee (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psc).
- AI: disclosure per the Sage policy (URL in the AI Policy table).
- Anonymisation: a separate title page is required and author names must be removed from the manuscript file, file name, headers and footers (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/psc).
- Independent-scholar or non-affiliated author rules: none stated on the journal's page; a web search for a Sage policy page on independent researchers returned none (2026-11-23).

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- A non-anonymised manuscript: the journal is double-anonymized and wants a separate title page (Peer Review table; Practical Concerns).
- Work outside scope: the guidelines state out-of-scope manuscripts will not be reviewed (Framing Requirements).
- Undisclosed generative-AI use beyond language and grammar help: the editor may reject at any stage (AI Policy table).

### Soft Tax

- Abstract must fit 100-150 words and the manuscript must be double-spaced with endnotes (Format table).
- A posted preprint can reveal identity to reviewers of a double-anonymized journal, and no updated preprint version may be posted during review (Preprint table).
- Timeline risk: the only data are self-reported (APA survey: average response 2.6 months, average publication time 8.6 months, mostly pre-2016 entries); no journal-stated timeline exists (Review Cycle Time).

### Best Suited For

- Theoretical and critical argument in social and political thought: "theoretic*|conceptual" in 20.3%, "critical theor*" in 9.8%, "histor*|genealog*" in 20.9% of 498 abstracts (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Work engaging Adorno, Marx, Hegel, Foucault, Arendt, Habermas or Rawls: each appears in 4.6-6.2% of abstracts (Epistemological Leanings).
- Single-voice, thesis-driven papers: "I" in 45.8% and "argu*" in 54.8% of abstracts (Voice & Style, Framing Requirements).

### Not Recommended For

- A stand-alone empirical study built on interviews, surveys or statistics: these terms appear in 0.4-0.6% of abstracts (Methodological Preferences); this is rarity, not a stated exclusion.
- Authors who need a published turnaround figure: the journal states none (Review Cycle Time).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Continental Philosophy Review](./continental-philosophy-review.md) | In the corpus; same continental-philosophy field, see that entry for its own data |
| 2 | [Inquiry](./inquiry-an-interdisciplinary-journal-of-philosophy.md) | In the corpus; broader interdisciplinary philosophy, see that entry for its own data |
| 3 | [Philosophy Today](./philosophy-today-an-international-journal-of-contemporary-philosophy.md) | In the corpus; contemporary continental philosophy, see that entry |

*(Fit reasoning is limited to topical overlap shown in the entries named; acceptance odds are not estimated.)*
